device.model: BDS-3 Classic 4-Channel Analog Drum Synthesizer with Special Effects Channel and Eurorack Format
device.category: 4-channel analogue drum synthesizer, desktop or 70 HP Eurorack
device.based_on: Simmons SDS-3 (late 1970s), per retailer descriptions; Behringer's own copy says only 'a classic drum synthesizer from the late 1970s'. Some early units are printed SDS-3.

sources.title: Behringer BDS-3 Quick Start Guide
sources.note: Multilingual; English controls, getting started, Eurorack installation and specifications used. The patch sheets are blank templates.

sources.title: Thomann and Musicorp product pages
sources.note: Original instrument (SDS-3), release (December 2025), and a user report of SDS-3 printed on early units.

architecture.patch_memory_note: No memory; settings are the panel. SynthTribe sets per-channel options.
architecture.summary: Four identical channels, each triggered by a microphone or other audio at its MIC IN (velocity sensitive) or by its own MIDI note. Each channel's tone comes from a self-oscillating diode ladder filter, mixed with filtered white noise, with an impact click, a pitch bend up or down into the set pitch, and a decay from 50 ms to 7 s. A master section holds overall pitch (with a pitch pedal), an LFO with an audio-rate FAST range, and RUN, a sample-and-hold stepped by channel triggers; each channel chooses whether these reach it and how strongly. Individual and mix outputs, MIDI and USB MIDI, decay kill footswitch.

modules.name: Channel 1 trigger
modules.description: Turns sound at MIC IN into a velocity-sensitive trigger once it passes MIC SENSITIVITY, or takes the channel's MIDI note. MIC OUT passes the microphone signal on.

modules.name: Channel 1 decay envelope
modules.description: Decay from 50 ms to 7 s on each trigger; also drives the bend and the impact click. Cut short by DECAY KILL.

modules.name: Channel 1 tone
modules.description: A self-oscillating diode ladder filter used as the tone oscillator, from below 20 Hz to over 30 kHz.

modules.name: Channel 1 noise
modules.description: White noise source.

modules.name: Channel 1 noise filter
modules.description: Filters the noise; PITCH opens it as it raises the tone.

modules.name: Channel 1 balance
modules.description: Balances tone and noise; equal at 12 o'clock.

modules.name: Channel 1 click filter
modules.description: Low-pass filter opened at the start of each hit by IMPACT CLICK, giving a stick-strike transient.

modules.name: Channel 1 VCA
modules.description: Shapes the channel with its decay; CHANNEL LEVEL sets both the channel output and its share of the mix.

behaviours.name: Triggering
behaviours.rule: Each channel fires from sound at its MIC IN once it passes MIC SENSITIVITY, louder sound giving a louder hit, or from its MIDI note (C1, D1, E1, F1 on the DIP-switch channel), with velocity setting loudness unless disabled in SynthTribe. MIC OUT passes the microphone on so the acoustic drum can still be recorded.

behaviours.name: Tone and noise
behaviours.rule: The tone is a self-oscillating diode ladder filter. PITCH sets its frequency and opens the noise filter together, so higher pitches give brighter noise. BALANCE mixes the two, from noise only to tone only.

behaviours.name: Bend
behaviours.rule: Each hit starts above (DOWN) or below (UP) the PITCH setting by BEND LEVEL and sweeps to it: the classic falling or rising synth-tom sweep. Fully anticlockwise gives a steady pitch.
behaviours.note: The guide says the pitch bends 'until the required frequency is reached'; the sweep following the decay envelope is assumed.

behaviours.name: Impact click
behaviours.rule: Adds a stick-like attack. Turning it up opens the low-pass cutoff at the start of the sound, making the click louder and brighter.

behaviours.name: Master effects
behaviours.rule: OVERALL PITCH scales every channel from 25% to 400%; at its centre the pitch pedal takes over. The LFO (square or sine, SLOW to 20 Hz or FAST to 4.3 kHz for FM-like tones) and RUN reach only channels with their switches on, by each channel's EFFECT RANGE.

behaviours.name: RUN
behaviours.rule: A sample and hold clocked by the triggers of RUN-enabled channels: each hit takes a new sample, so successive hits step through values. RUN TIME sets how many samples are taken before the sampled wave resets.
behaviours.note: What is sampled is not stated.

behaviours.name: Decay kill
behaviours.rule: The DECAY KILL footswitch or MIDI CC 80 overrides DECAY TIME and cuts the sound off, on channels enabled in SynthTribe.

behaviours.name: Warm-up
behaviours.rule: Allow 15 minutes or more, longer from cold, before recording or performance.

midi.channel_note: Receive channel 1-16 set by rear DIP switches; MIDI THRU mirrors MIDI IN; USB MIDI is class compliant.
midi.note: Note-number octave convention for C1 is not stated (36 under the C1 = 36 convention, 24 under C-1 = 0).

specifications.oscillators: 4 self-oscillating diode ladder filters / 4 x white noise

how the bend is generated and its time

the noise filter's type and slope
source_inconsistencies: The title promises a 'Special Effects Channel', but the guide describes four channels and a master/effects section, not a fifth channel.
The TRIGGER LED description refers to triggers 'over MIDI (3)', but callout 3 is the MIC OUT socket.
Dimensions are 95 x 375 x 136 mm in the guide and 374 x 136 x 93 mm on Thomann.

modelling_gaps.detail: A quick start guide only. The signal order (mix, click filter, VCA) and the modulation destinations are inferred from control descriptions.
The Simmons SDS-3 attribution comes from retailers, not Behringer; an original SDS-3 manual or schematic would settle the inferred structure.
Per-channel pitch, velocity and decay kill settings exist in the app; further app-only options may follow firmware updates.
